claim_summary: The work contributes model-aware numerical time-series encoding and continuous-density conversion of autoregressive token probabilities for zero-shot probabilistic forecasting.

claim_evidence.quote: By encoding time series as a string of numerical digits, we can frame time series forecasting as next-token prediction in text.
this performance, we propose procedures for effectively tokenizing time series data and converting discrete distributions over tokens into highly flexible densities over continuous values.

modules.name: Decimal time-series encoding and rescaling
modules.scope_reason: R2 places this on the LLM side because it changes model-facing numerical input representation. Counterfactually, as Harness logic it would involve temporal numerical data (GTS), without embedding a task-family objective (not TSK); its actual locus is model representation.

evidence.quote: Tokenization is particularly important because it directly influences how patterns form within tokenized sequences and the types of operations that language models can learn.
Rescaling To avoid wasting tokens when the inputs are very large, we scale values down so that the α-percentile of rescaled time series values is 1.

modules.name: Continuous density adaptation from token probabilities
modules.scope_reason: R2 places this on the LLM side because it transforms the model's discrete numerical-token output distribution into a continuous forecast density. Counterfactually, as Harness logic it would involve temporal numerical data (GTS), without embedding a task-family objective (not TSK); its actual locus is model output representation.

evidence.quote: Autoregressive models over sequences of digits act like hierarchical softmax distributions over the corresponding numbers. When combined with uniform distributions in each discrete bucket, distributions over strings can become expressive distributions over continuous domains.
